title: Zoned VPC network fabric Terraform module with per-AZ NAT, endpoints, and health checks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: ship a reusable Terraform module that provisions a production-ready VPC network fabric tailored for Redwood Private deployments. The module should support: zonal subnet groups (control, app, db), per-AZ NAT gateways (or NAT gatewayless pattern via EIP pools), IGW for public subnets, configurable VPC endpoints (S3, ECR, STS, Secrets Manager), route table orchestration, and automated health checks + replacement logic for NAT/endpoint failures.

Scope and constraints:
- Inputs: number_of_azs, cidr_blocks per AZ, nat_mode (zonal|shared), endpoint_whitelist, enable_flow_logs, private_dns_for_endpoints.
- Outputs: subnet ids grouped by purpose, route table ids, nat gateway ids, endpoint ids, example security group id for control-plane.
- Module must be cloud-agnostic within AWS account boundaries (no cross-account resources created).
- Must support strict corporate IP ranges and optional customer-supplied route-propagation to on-prem routers.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Per-AZ NAT gateways increase cost but reduce cross-AZ egress and improve failover isolation. For cost-sensitive customers we expose nat_mode=zonal|shared and document expected unit economics.
- Use managed VPC endpoints for S3 & ECR to avoid egress; support prefix lists for more advanced controls but keep default simple.
- Health checks: implement Lambda-backed periodic probes (Terraform module deploys CloudWatch Event Rule -> Lambda) that validates endpoint reachability and verifies NAT latency thresholds. On failure, we emit metrics and optionally trigger an SSM Automation or Terraform runbook via Step Functions. This keeps in-module automation minimal while enabling ops workflows.
- Upgrades: follow a 3-stage rollout: dry-run plan in customer sandbox, canary apply to a non-critical AZ pair, full apply. Module follows semantic versioning; breaking changes require migration helper scripts included in /scripts/migrate-*.sh.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module passes terratest suite (integration) across 2/3 AZ matrix with nat_mode=zonal and nat_mode=shared.
- Health check Lambda emits metrics to /redwood/vpc/network-health and creates an alarm which is wired to the customer's PagerDuty integration by default.
- End-to-end test: deployment with a sample Private workload (nginx) successfully reaches S3/ECR without egress and recovers within 3 minutes when we simulate NAT failure.

Operational playbook (high-level):
- If a NAT GW alarm fires, run the included runbook which will (1) collect NAT and route metrics, (2) attempt replacement (allocate new EIP + create replacement NAT), (3) update route table and drain affected subnets.
- Automated snapshot of route tables and endpoints every 24h stored in S3 for post-mortem.

Compatibility and security:
- Module enforces TLS-only endpoint configs and supports KMS key ARN for flow log encryption.
- IAM least-privilege role example included for CI pipelines that apply the module.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module under infra/modules/vpc-fabric with README, examples/ (default, nat-shared, restricted-endpoint), and scripts/ for migrations.
- Terratest integration tests and a lightweight local acceptance harness in /test/acceptance.
- Design doc and runbook in Confluence.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge module to feature branch and run CI terratest in staging AWS accounts.
2) Internal canary apply to infra-dev workspace (non-production) week of 2026-03-15.
3) Customer pilot with one Private deployment (security reviewed) week of 2026-03-22.

Notes: coordinate with Network Security for prefix-list quotas and with SRE for PagerDuty alarm bindings.
